items.title: Ask Camp
items.description: Conversational front door that lets prospective families ask a camp anything and get grounded answers, launched as the first parent-facing modernization surface.
items.problemStatement: Prospective families bounce between static FAQ pages and email to get basic questions answered before registration, and camps field the same questions by hand every season.

kr.statement: Deflect at least 40% of pre-registration inbound questions to self-serve answers within a season.

items.outcomeReading: Deflected 44% of pre-registration questions in the first season, beating the 40% target. Kept as the pattern for later conversational surfaces.
items.whatWeLearned: Families will trust an AI front door when answers are grounded in the camp's own content and cite where they came from — ungrounded answers tanked trust in early tests.
items.whatWeDoDifferently: Ship the citation/grounding UI on day one next time instead of bolting it on after the first trust dip.
items.nextBet: Reuse the grounded-answer pattern for a returning-family surface (session changes, forms status), not just prospective families.
activity: Shipped as the first parent-facing modernization surface.
Outcome reading recorded against the deflection KR.

items.title: AskCamp
items.description: First internal AI assistant surface (AskCamp), proving out grounded question-answering on camp data.
items.problemStatement: Support and product teams had no grounded way to query camp data in natural language, so answers meant hand-written SQL and tribal knowledge.

kr.statement: Answer at least 60% of internal data questions without a hand-written query.
kr.metric: Internal data questions answered without hand-written SQL

items.outcomeReading: Answered 63% of internal data questions without SQL. Validated the grounding approach reused by AskMinder.
items.whatWeLearned: Internal users ask far broader questions than the SQL-replacement framing assumed; the grounding layer mattered more than query coverage.
items.whatWeDoDifferently: Instrument unanswered questions from week one so the gap between asked and answerable is visible, rather than inferring it later.
items.nextBet: Extend the shared grounding approach to AskMinder's staff-facing reporting flows.
activity: Shipped as the AI platform's first grounded surface.

items.title: Registration Modernization — MVP → GA
items.description: The current-quarter push to get modern, mobile-first registration into camps' hands: first MVP in early August, GA targeted for early-to-mid September. Precursor to the FY27-Q1 Registration + Season Admin GA.
items.problemStatement: Families register on a dated, desktop-oriented flow while camps need a modern registration experience in time for the next enrollment cycle; scope confidence has wavered and some infrastructure/delivery timelines have slipped.

kr.statement: Ship the registration MVP by early August and reach GA by mid-September.
kr.metric: Registration modernization milestones hit on schedule

items.title: AskCamp polish + public launch
items.description: Polishing the AskCamp parent-facing experiences and the underlying AI nodes ahead of a public launch announcement — the productization of the AskCamp pilot that shipped last quarter.
items.problemStatement: AskCamp proved the grounded-answer pattern as a pilot, but the parent-facing experiences and AI nodes need polish and a coordinated launch before it can be marketed as a real product surface.

items.title: Enrollment reporting MVP on Databricks
items.description: A deliberately small first bet on the modern data stack: a dev Databricks instance (pay-as-you-go) pulling enrollment data into a simple MVP dashboard. Precursor to the FY27-Q1 Data Lake & AI-reporting V1.
items.problemStatement: Camps and leadership lack a modern, self-serve view of enrollment; reporting today is locked in the monolith. A small dashboard on a stood-up data stack tests the pipeline end to end before the larger data-lake investment.

items.title: Customer Love Tiger Team (Summer '26)
items.description: A dedicated team shipping the highest-impact bugs and small features for at-risk camps through the summer, containing customer interruptions so the modernization teams stay protected. Folds back into Delta on ~Sept 1.
items.problemStatement: Reactive customer issues threaten churn (particularly from Campfront) before summer and pull focus off modernization. A focused team absorbs the quick-win work so the rest of the org can show modernization results in late summer and fall.

kr.statement: Keep at-risk camps satisfied through summer and limit customer-issue interruptions to this team.
kr.metric: Modernization teams shielded from customer-issue interruptions

items.title: UltraCamp new payment processor rollout
items.description: Payments integration (Paysafe + Rainforest) engineering is complete; the payments team now owns rolling out and migrating all UltraCamp customers to the new processor by a mid-August hard deadline.
items.problemStatement: UltraCamp customers need to be migrated off the legacy payment integration onto the new Paysafe + Rainforest processor before the mid-August deadline, without disrupting in-season payments.

kr.statement: Migrate all UltraCamp customers to the new payment processor by mid-August.
kr.metric: UltraCamp customers migrated to the new processor
